{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built stroke 4, the lower tail of our fish, and it came out connected and dark from the start. I kept the tip soft and curved, as the design called for, so the fall carried through without stalling. The tail is a big part of what makes the outline read as a fish rather than a blob. The final check showed the whole picture, all 118 dominoes, falling from the nose.

Execution: I started on my stroke as soon as the sketch was on the pad and laid it in steady batches until it was finished. I then inspected the tail area closely several times, including the joins around the fork, to confirm the chain was unbroken. Once everything was connected I kept my hands off the table, so I didn't risk a bump or knock anything over before the push.

Collaboration: I told the table when I started, when my piece was done, and what I'd checked. I offered to take the last stretch down to the notch if Omar wanted help, and otherwise kept clear of his corner. Working on separate parts of the fish meant nobody got in anyone else's way. I made a point of recognizing teammates' good work and kept the mood light.

Leadership: I took ownership of my piece without needing direction and reported its status clearly, so others could plan around it. I helped keep the table disciplined late on, with hands off and no unnecessary tinkering, which protected a working result. I think I contributed about a quarter of the table's result: a full, reliable stroke of the tail plus verification, in a team effort.", "my_share_percent": 25}
